title: OOP
content:
Object-oriented programming is a programming paradigm that organizes code around objects.
Objects are self-contained units that bundle data and functions together.
An object oriented program is basically a collection of objects and relationships among them.
Objects communicate or interact with each other using message passing.
This approach uses concepts like:
  • Classes (templates for objects)
  • Encapsulation (bundling data and methods)
  • Inheritance (reusing properties from other classes)
  • Polymorphism (objects taking on many forms) to create modular, reusable, extensible and generic software system.

title: OOP
content:
Object-oriented Programming
Object-oriented programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that organizes code around objects, which are self-contained units that bundle data and functions together. This approach uses concepts like classes (templates for objects), encapsulation (bundling data and methods), inheritance (reusing properties from other classes), and polymorphism (objects taking on many forms) to create modular, reusable, and maintainable code. An object oriented program is basically a collection of objects and relationships among them and they communicate or interact with each other using message passing. Four main concept of OOPs are abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism which help us to write modular, reusable, extensible and generic software system.
Classes and Objects
A class body contains contains specification of a set of fields which defines attributes of the objects and a set of methods which defines behaviours of the objects. Class is the unit of modularization in object oriented program. A class is a blueprint which defines the attributes (fields) and behaviours (methods) common to a number of objects. A class is a user defined blueprint based on which objects are created. Object is a concrete entity with a set of attributes and a set of behaviours. Object also have identify, lifetime and scope and belongs to a class. Fields defines the attributes of objects instantiated from a class. Methods defines the behaviors of objects instantiated from a class. Objects maintain state in instance variables (attributes). Objects are allocated from the heap and accessed by reference variables. Objects communicates with one another by sending and receiving message.
CodeDesc
class Snake { Size size; Color color; Point position; void move(Dir dir) {} void eat(Food food) {} } Defines attributes and behaviours of snakes. Behaviours are used to change states. State is combination of attributes values. Attributes = {size, color, position} Behaviours = {move, eat} Attributes = Form
Encapsulation
Encapsulation is the process of wrapping of related data and code into a single unit which modularizes our software system. Encapsulation also help us to achieve data hiding which is the process of hiding sensitive data of the objects from the outside world. Encapsulation refers to the bundling of data with the mechanisms or methods that operate on the data. Encapsulation also refer to the limiting of direct access to some of that data, such as an object's components. Essentially encapsulation prevents external code from being concerned with the internal workings of an object. Encapsulation is java is achieved through class. Encapsulation makes out software system modular ie. we can change one part of the code without affecting other parts of code. Data hiding is the process of hiding sensitive data of the object from the user of the object. Data hiding is a programming concept which protects the data from direct modification by other parts of the program. Data hiding is achieved by declaring fields as private and providing setter and getter methods for each field to access and update the value. Data hiding is closely related to abstraction and encapsulation. Data hiding is achieved through encapsulation. Advantages of encapsulation:
  • Data security: help us to make fields of a class read-only or write-only.
  • Encapsulation gives a clear and modular structure to our software system.
  • Program is well organized so easy to maintain.
Inheritance
Inheritance is a mechanism by which one class acquires the attributes (fields) and functionalities (methods) of another existing class. This mechanism promotes code reusability and establishes a hierarchical is-a relationship between classes. Reusability helps us to avoid duplicate code and data. Inheritance helps us to define relationship among classes. Inheritance enable us to create modules that does not need to be changed when new attributes or functionalities is added to the class. Kind of inheritance:
  • Single inheritance - when a class inherits another class.
  • Multi-level inheritance - when a class inherits derived class.
  • Hierarchical inheritance - when a class is inherited by many classes.
Abstraction
Abstraction is a mechanism of hiding unnecessary details and showing only essential details to the user by separating interface from its implementation. Abstraction also generalises by capturing the common essense among unrelated classes. Main goal of the abstraction it to reduce the complexity of the design and implementation process of software system. Abstraction can be achieved through interface and abstract class. Abstract method is a method that is declared without implementation. Abstract method must always be redefined in the subclass. Abstract method only have signature. Abstract method can not be final. Class which contains abstract method must be declared abstract. Abstract class is one of two ways to achieve abstraction in Java. Abstract class declared with abstract keyword. Abstract class cannot be instanciated. Abstract class cannot be final. Abstract class always have a default constructor. Abstract class can have parameterized constructors. Abstract class is created to be extended or inherited. Abstract class can have abstract and non-abstract methods. A class that extends an abstract class must implement all its abstract method. Interface is one of two ways to achieve abstraction in java. Interface is completely abstract class. Interface methods are by default abstract and public. Interface variables are by default public, static and final. Interface specifies only what needs to be done. Childrens will decide how to do in their own way. Like abstract class interface cannot be instanciated. Interface allows us to group several related classes as siblings. Method = Method header + method body. Method header is an abstraction of a block of code. Abstract method is independent of implementation which can have many implementations. Abstraction: Complete abstraction can be achieved through interface. Security: Hides implementation details and only show the important details of an object. Multiple inheritance: Can be achieved through interface because a class can implements multiple interfaces.
Interface

Polymorphism
Polymorphism refers to one-to-many relationship, which allows an entity such as an variable, a method or an object to have more than one form. Polymorphism enables us to deal with generalities and let the compiler and runtime environment to handle the specific. Polymorphism in Java can be achieved through method overloading, method overriding and Generics. Polymorphism is the provision of a single interface to entities of different types or the use of a single symbol to represent multiple different types. Field level polymorphism: a reference variable of class T can point to object of class E as well as object of subclass of E. Many methods can have one common name.
  • One method can accept many types of arguments.
  • One method header can be associated with many method body.
  • One type of reference variable can be used to access many type of objects.
Subtype-polymorphism
Subtype polymorphism is a form of type polymorphism where a variable of a superclass type refer to and object of a subclass type, allowing a single interface to represent different type of objects. Which means code written for a superclass can be used with instances of its subclasses and at runtime, the program calls the correct method based on the object's actual type. Inheritance and substitutability - a subclass is considered a subtype of its superclass. This relationship allows an object of the subclass to be substituted for an object of the superclass. Dynamic method selection - the specific method tha is executed is determined at runtime, not at compile time. Single interface for multiple types - this allows us to write code that operates on superclass type and have it work correctly with any of its subclasses.
Method-overloading
Process of writing multiple methods with the same name in the same class is called method overloading. Method-overloading is a kind of static polymorphism.
  • Method overloading increases the readability of the program.
  • Avoids the need to memorize multiple method names.
  • Method overloading makes our code more generic.
  • Method overloading support clean code.
  • The complexity of the code is reduced.
  • Compiler binds the method call with an approriate method body.
Method overloading is achieved by:
  • Changing the number of arguments.
  • Changing the data type of the arguments.
Method-overriding
Method-overriding is the process of redefining a parent class instance method into its child class is known as method overriding. An instance method defined in the parent class is redefined into its child class to give specific implementation of the parent class method. Referenced object type, not the reference variable type determines which method will be called. When we create a parent class reference variable and assign a child class object then calling an overridden method on that variable will call the child class behaviour.
  • Final methods can not be overridden.
  • Static methods can not be overridden.
  • Private methods can not be overridden.
  • Child class method is called overriding method.
  • Parent class method is called overridden method.
  • Overridden methods are dynamically dispatched.
  • Finalize method can be overridden to free system resources.
  • Overridden parent class method can be called using super keyword.
  • Runtime polymorphism can be achieved through method overriding.
  • Abstract methods can only be overridden by the first concrete class.
  • The access level cannot be more restrictive than the overridden method.
  • Override annotation denotes that the method overrides the base class method.
Later Binding
Dynamic binding is a process in which a call to overridden method is resolved at the runtime rather than compile time. Which means that the code to be executed for a specific method call is not known until runtime. Dynamic dispatch is used when multiple classes contain different implementations of the same method which provides a mechanism for selecting the function to be executed from various function alternatives at the runtime. Dynamic binding (dispatch) is the process of linking function call to a specific sequence of code (function) at run-time.
Association
Association represents a relationship where one object is linked to another object. Association describes relationships between classes. The association can be one-way or two-way. Which implies that two classes are related, but neither class owns the other. Associations relate entities that can exist independently of each other - such as authors and books.
Aggregation
Aggregation is a special form of association where one object contains another object. However, the contained object can exist independently of the container. Lifetime of the contained object is not dependent on the lifetime of the container. Aggregation represents has-a relationship between objects. Composition represents part-of relationship between objects. An aggregation is a collection or the gathering of things together. Aggregation - A has an instance of B, B can exists without A. Composition - A has an instance of B, B cannot exists without A.
Composition
Composition is a stronger form of association where one object contains another object and the contained object cannot exist independently of the container. The lifetime of the contained object depends on the lifetime of the container. In composition if owning object is garbage collected the owned object will also be which is not the case in aggregation. Composition means the child entity (order items) is part of a whole and cannot exist independently of the parent entity (order). The child entity is contained in the parent entity and can only be accessed via the parent entity. Both composition and aggregation express a has-a relationship. Composition expresses a strong has-a relationship (whole-part ownership); aggregation expresses a weak has-a relationship (association without ownership).
Composition vs Inheritance
Both composition and inheritance used to solve the same problem that is code reuse. Process of building complex objects from simpler ones is called object composition. Use inheritance only when you want both hierarchical reuse of code and subtype polymorphism.
Dependency Injection
Dependency injection generally means passing a dependent object as a parameter to a method rather than having the method create the dependent object. Dependency injection is a software design pattern that allow us to develop loosely-coupled software. Dependecy injection allows us to depends more on abstraction rather than the concrete implementation, which promotes loosely-coupled architecture, flexibility and pluggability within our code. What it means in practice is that the method does not have a direct dependency on a particular implementation, any implementation that meets the requirements can be passed as a parameter. Dependency injection is a programming technique where an object or function receives its dependencies (other objects or functions it needs) from an external source, rather than creating them itself. This approach, which is a form of Inversion of Control, makes code more flexible, maintainable, and testable by decoupling components and allowing them to be replaced or mocked easily.
SOLID
Solid principle is a set of guidelines for writing code that makes it easier to manage, extend and debug. Solid principle help us break big problem into smaller easier to handle parts. Solid reduces dependencies on code so changes in one area won't break another. Solid reduces tight coupling, making code more flexible and easier to maintain.

title: Java
content:
Java
Java is a high-level, general purpose, object-oriented, generic, concurrent and functional programming language. Java enables programmer to write once, run anywhere (WORA), meaning compiled java code can run on all platform without the need to recompile. Java applications are typically compiled to bytecode that can run on any JVM regardless of the underlying computer architecture. Java runtime provides dynamic capabilities such as reflection and runtime code modification that are typically not available in traditional compiled languages. Object-oriented: Java is a complete object-oriented programming language. Multithreaded: Java has support for multithreading at the language level. Dynamic: Java support dynamic code modification through reflection. Simple: Java is simple and easy to learn. Portable: Java program is compiled to bytecode insted of machine code. Secure: Because execution of bytecode is under the control of the JVM. Compiled and interpreted: Java program is compiled then interpreted by the JVM. High performance:Java bytecode executes with high performance because of JIT. Platform independent: Java is independent of operating system platform. Architecture neutral: Java is independent of hardware platform.
Java Developement Kit
Java development kit is collection of tools which is used to compile, debug and run a program developed using the java technology. JDK is the superset of JRE which is superset of JVM. JDK includes a JRE, a compiler, a debugger, an archiver and other tools that are used in Java development. javac: Compiler that read Java source code and translates them into bytecode which is executed by the JVM. javadoc: Documentation generator that read Java source code and generates documentation. javap: Disassembler that is used to disassemble Java class file. jdb: Debugger command-line debugging tool used to find and fix bugs in Java programs. jar: Archiver general purpose Java archiver.
Java Virtual Machine
Java virtual machine is an abstract computing machine which loads, verifies and executes bytecode. Bytecode is the instruction set of the java virtual machine. Java virtual machine is divided into three main subsystem:
  • Class loader subsystem
  • Runtime data area
  • Execution engine
Verify: Bytecode verifier will verify whether the generated bytecode is proper or will get the verification error.
Prepare: All static variables memory will be allocated and assigned with default values.
Resolve: All symbolic memory references are replaced with the original references from method area.
Class-loader
Class loader subsystem is responsible for loading, linking, verifying and initializing java class file. Runtime data areas contain class area, heap area, stack areas and PC registers. Execution engine contains an bytecode interpreter, JIT compiler and memory manager. The class loader is part of the java virtual machine which is used to load class files during execution of a program. Application classes and all the dependencies from imported JARs are loaded by the system class loader. Bootstrap class loader loads JDK core classes (rt.jar). Extension class loader loads classes defined in lib\ext directory. System class loader loads classes from the classpath. Custom class loader loads classes from third party libraries.
Java Memory
Class Area - Class elements like constant pool, class fields, constructor codes, method codes are stored here. All executing threads share this part of the JVM memory area. Heap - Heap is the area of memory where states of the each objects are stored. Heap memory is not thread-safe as it is shared by all threads of a program. Heap is dynamic area of memory. Stack - Stack memory stores information about the active methods of a java program which grows and shrinks as new methods are added and removed to stack memory. Stack memory gets automatically allocated and deallocated. Access to stack memory is fast as compared to heap memory. Stack memory is thread-safe as each thread has its own stack memory. Native Stack - Stack memory stores information about the active native methods. PC Registers - PC registers stores the address of currently executing instruction.
Constant Pool
Constant pool is a part of .class file that contains constants needed to run the code of that class. These constants include literals specified by the programmer and symbolic references generated by compiler. Symbolic references are basically names of fields, methods and classes referenced from the code. These references are used by the linker to link our code. System.out.println("Hello, world!"); 0: getstatic #2 3: ldc #3 5: invokevirtual #5 #2 Field java/lang/System.out:Ljava/io/PrintStream; #3 String Hello, world! #5 Method java/io/PrintStream.println:(Ljava/lang/String;)V
Local Variable
Variable declared inside method is called local variable. Local variables are stored on stack. Local variables must be initialized before first use. Local variables can only be accessed by the code inside the method. Memory for local variable is allocated when corresponding method is called. Local vars exist only while the method in which they are declared is executing.
Instance Variable
Instance variables are declared inside class and outside method. Instance variables are initialized to their default values. Instance variables are stored in the heap area of memory. Instance variables represents state of the object. Instance variables are accessed using object of the class. Instance variables can not be accessed directly from static context. Instance variables are created when an object of the class is created. Instance variables are destroyed when the object is destroyed. Each objects of a class have separate copy of the instance variables.
Static Variable
Static variables are created inside class and outside method with static keyword. Static variables are stored in the class area of the java virtual machine. Static variables are initialized only once when the class is loaded. Static variables belongs to the class and not to object. Static variables can be accessed directly by the class name. Lifetime of an static variable is the same as the lifetime of the program. Static variables can be accessed by both instance method and static method. Memory allocation only happens once when the class is loaded in the memory.
Static Block
The static block is a block of statement inside a java class that will be executed when a class is first loaded into the JVM. A static block helps to initialize the static data members just like constructors helps us to initialize instance members. A static block executes once in the life cycle of any program, another property of static block is that it executes before the main method. Instance initialization blocks are used to initialize the instance data members. Instance initialization blocks runs each time a new instance is created. Instance initialization blocks comes in the order in which they appear. Order of execution:
  • Instance initialization block of the superclass.
  • Constructors of the superclass.
  • Instance initialization blocks of the class.
  • Constructors of the class.
Method
Methods are used to perform a simple task of the program. Method header provides interface to the other methods. Methods form the object's interface with the outside world. Objects define their interaction with the outside world through the methods that they expose. Method has two parts one is header (interface) and other is body (implementation). Instance method is a method that belongs to instances of a class. Instance method defines behaviour of the objects. Instance method can be overriden, abstract and concrete. Instance method can refer to this and super keyword. Instance method can not be accessed from the static context. Instance method can access instance variables, static variables, instance methods and static methods. Static method is a method which belongs to the class and not to the object. Static method can not access instance variables or methods of the class. Static method can only access static variables or methods of the class. Static method is associated with the class in which it is defined. Static method cannot refer to this or super keyword. Static method is statically bound to method call. Static method can be accessed directly by the class name without any object.
Autoboxing and Unboxing
Automatic conversion of primitive types to corresponding wrapper class is known as autoboxing. Automatic conversion of wrapper class to corresponding primitive types is known as unboxing. Autoboxing and unboxing is performed at compile time by compiler. Java compiler applies autoboxing when a primitive value:
  • Assigned to a variable of the corresponding wrapper class.
  • Passed as param to a method that expects an object of the corresponding wrapper class.
Java compiler applies unboxing when a wrapper class object:
  • Assigned to a variable of the corresponding primitive type.
  • Passed as param to a method that expects an argument of corresponding primitive type.
Access Modifiers
Access modifiers are used for defining accessibility of classes, methods and fields. default: Declarations are visible only within the package. private: Declarations are visible within the class only. protected: Declarations are visible within the package or all subclasses. public: Declarations are visible everywhere. Class modifiers:
  • final: Class cannot be inherited by other classes.
  • abstract: Class cannot be used to create objects.
Method modifiers:
  • final: Method cannot be overridden or modified.
  • static: Method belongs to the class rather than an object.
  • abstract: Method does not have a body which is provided by the subclass.
  • synchronized: Method can only be accessed by one thread at a time.
Field modifiers:
  • final: Field cannot be modified.
  • static: Field belongs to the class rather than an object.
  • transient: Fields are skipped when serializing the object containing them.
  • volatile: Field value is not cached thread-locally and is always read from the memory.
Constructor
Constructor is a kind of method that is used to initialize newly created objects. Constructor has the same name as the class name in which it is declared. Constructor is automatically called upon creation of a new object. Constructor cannot be abstract, static, final and synchronized. Constructor can be overloaded. Constructor can not have return type. Constructor can be parameterized or can have zero parameter. Constructor with zero parameter is known as default constructor. Constructor overloading is the special kind of method overloading. Parent class constructor is called before the subclass constructor is called. The process of calling a constructor from another constructor is called constructor chaining. Expose multiple ways of constructing an object using constructors chaining. Constructor chaining makes our code more readable and avoid duplicate code. Constructor chaining can be done in two ways:
  • By using this keyword for chaining constructors in the same class.
  • By using super keyword for chaining constructors from the parent class.
Immutable Class
An immutable class is a class whose instances cannot be modified after they are created. Once an object of an immutable class is initialized, its state remains constant throughout its lifetime. Immutable class is good for multithreaded application as state of the object cannot be changed.
  • Make all fields final and private.
  • Do not provide setter mathods.
  • Declare class as final to prevent subclasses to override methods.
  • The constructor is responsible for setting the initial state of the object.
  • When the instance fields include references to mutable objects:
  • Performs a deep copy of these mutable objects to prevent external references from modifying the internal state.
  • Getter methods for these mutable objects also return deep copies or unmodifiable views rather than direct references to the internal mutable objects. This prevents external code from obtaining a reference and altering the internal state.
Exception
Exception is an event that disrupts the normal flow of a program during its execution. When an exception occurs, the program's normal execution path is interrupted and the Java virtual machine (JVM) attempts to find an appropriate exception handler to manage the error. If no handler is found, the program terminates. Exception can be divided into two board categories: faults introduced by the programmer, such as division by zero or calling a method with null reference and things out of the programmer's control, such as a user entering a garbage on the keyboard when the program expects a positive integer. Try-catch and finally blocks helps in writing the application code which may throw exceptions at runtime and gives us a chance to either recover from exception by executing alternate application logic or handle the exception to report back to the user. Which helps in preventing the ugly application crashes. Try-catch promotes separation of concern principles by avoiding mixing of business logic code and error handling code.
  • Code to be monitored for exceptions is written inside try block.
  • Catch block contains exception handling code.
  • We can use multiple catch with a single try.
  • Catch block must be written next to the try block.
  • Finally statement defines a code block to run regardless of the result.
Facts about Exception
Checked exceptions are those checked by the java compiler at compile time. Checked exceptions are forced to be caught or declared by the compiler. Checked exceptions are also called compile time exceptions. Checked exceptions can be handled. Checked exceptions can be propagated through throws. Code will not compile if checked exceptions are not handled. Checked exception represent a potential problem that the user knows can happen. Checked exception forces the user to establish an error handling policy at compile time. Unchecked exceptions are not checked by the compiler at compile time. Unchecked exceptions are also called RuntimeExceptions or Error. Unchecked exceptions does not need to be caught or declared. Unchecked exceptions are caught by the JVM. Unchecked exceptions can not be handled. Runtime exception indicates an issue with the code that can be prevented. Unchecked exceptions represent an unexpected defect in the application that happens at runtime. Unchecked exceptions does not force the user to establish an error handling policy on compile.
Lambda
Lambda is a concise way to represent anonymous functions which is primarily used to implement functional interfaces. Lambda expressions are similar to methods but without name and they can be defined inside the body of a method. Lambda enable functional programming paradigms in Java, allowing behavior (functions) to be passed as arguments to methods or assigned to variables. The lambda expression should have the same number of parameters and the same return type as that method. Lambda expression help us to avoid boilerplate code. Supplier randomValue = () -> Math.random(); System.out.println(randomValue.get()); Predicate<Integer> lessThan = a -> (a < 100); System.out.println(lessThan.test(101)); Consumer<String> consumer = a -> System.out.println(a); list.stream().forEach(consumer); Function<String, String> function = a -> a.toUpperCase(); System.out.println(function.apply("hello"));
Serialization
Serialization is the process of converting an object into stream of bytes. Once we have a stream of bytes we can store that into database, memory or into a file. Serialization is done to persist data or state of an object beyond the life cycle of an application. Second reason to serialize an object is to transmit data or state of an object over a network. All subtypes of a serializable class are also serializable. Serializable interface has no methods or fields and serves only to identify the semantic of being serializable. Serializability of a class is enabled by the class implementing the io.Serializable interface. Classes that do not implement this interface will not have any of their state serialized or deserialized. User user = new User("Aryan", "aryan@gmail.com", 10) FileOutputStream fos = new FileOutputStream("usr.d") ObjectOutputStream oos = new ObjectOutputStream(fos) oos.writeObject(user) oos.close() fos.close()
Deserialization
Deserialization is the process of reconstructing an object that has been serialized before. Deserialization is the reverse process of serialization where byte stream is used to create actual java object into memory. Transient keyword is used to avoid serialization of particular field of an serializable object. Fields marked with transient will not be serialized during serialization. Deserialization process would use the default values for such fields when creating an object out of the serialized form bacause transient fields are not present in the serialized form of an object. FileInputStream fis = new FileInputStream("usr.d") ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(fis) User user = (User) ois.readObject() ois.close() fis.close()

title: SOLID
content:
Solid principle is a set of guidelines for writing code that makes it easier to manage, extend and debug.
Solid principle help us break big problem into smaller easier to handle parts.
Solid reduces dependencies on code so changes in one area won't break another.
Solid reduces tight coupling, making code more flexible and easier to maintain.

title: Design Patterns
content:
Design patterns are reusable solutions to commonly occurring problems in software design.
Design patterns are solutions or techniques to avoid code design problem.
Design patterns help us write robust, clean, modular and extensible code.
Design patterns provide a template for solving design issues in various contexts.
Design patterns help us write robust, clean, modular, maintainable, scalable and understandable and extensible code.

Design patterns are divided into three categories:
  • Creational patterns - Deals with object creation.
  • Structural patterns - Deals with object composition.
  • Behavioral Patterns - Deals with object interaction and responsibility.
Advantages
Reusability Provide a reusable solution to common software design problems which saves developers from reinventing the wheel whenever they encounter a new problem. Instead, they can use a tried and tested pattern to solve the problem. Maintainability Promote clean, organized and maintainable code which makes it easier for developers to maintain and modify the code as the software evolves. Rapid-developement Provide a standard way of solving common software design problems which saves time and effort in the desing and development process, allowing developers to focus on other aspects of the software.

Creational: Singleton, Builder, Factory Method, Abstract Factory and Prototype.
Structural: Adapter, Bridge, Composite, Decorator, Facade, Flyweight and Proxy.
Behavioral: CoR, Command, Iterator, Mediator, Memento, Observer, State, Strategy, Template and Visitor.

title: Adapter
content:
Adapter pattern is a structural design pattern that allows objects with incompatible interfaces to work together.
Adapter acts as a bridge between two incompatible interfaces.
Adapter pattern converts the interface of a class into another interface that the client expects.
Adapter lets classes work together that couldn’t otherwise because of incompatible interfaces.
Adapter catches calls for one object and transforms them to format and interface recognizable by the second object.
Adapter pattern should be used when:
  • There is an existing class and its interface does not match the one you need.
  • We need to connect systems or components that were not built to work together.
Components:
  • Target: The interface the client expects.
  • Adaptee: The existing class that needs adapting.
  • Adapter: The class that implements the target interface and internally uses or adapts the adaptee.
Pros and Cons:
  • Reusability of existing functionality.
  • Keeps existing code untouched.
  • Code can become complex if many adapters are introduced.
  • Sometimes it's better to refactor than use adapters excessively.

title: Facade
content:
Facade pattern is a structural design pattern that provides a unified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem.
A complex interface to the client is considered as a fault in the design of a system.
Facade defines a higher-level interface that makes the subsystem easier to use.
Facade pattern makes a complex interface easier to use using a Facade class.

When-to use:
  • When you want to simplify the usage of a complex system.
  • When there are multiple subsystems that need to be integrated.
  • To decouple clients from the internal components of a system.
  • When you want to create a layered architecture.
Advantages:
  • Simplifies complex interfaces.
  • Makes the system easier to use.
  • Promotes loose coupling.
  • Improves code readability.

title: Composite
content:
Composite: kind of structural design pattern used when we want to treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly.
This is especially useful when you deal with hierarchical tree structures, such as file systems, DOM tree or UI components.
Composite lets clients treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly.

When-to use:
  • When we want to compose objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies.
Components:
  • Component: interface or abstract class for all objects in the hierarchy, both composite and leaf.
  • Leaf: represents individual objects (end nodes) which implements the base Component.
  • Composite: a container that holds child Components.
  • Client: uses the Component interface to interact with objects in the hierarchy uniformly.
Use cases:
  • GUI frameworks (Swing or HTML DOM trees)
  • Organization hierarchy (employees, managers)
  • File system (files and directories)
  • Document structures (paragraphs, sections, characters)

title: Proxy
content:
Proxy pattern is a structural design pattern that provides a proxy for other objects to control access to them.
Proxy implements the same interface as the real object and can add behavior like access control, logging, caching, lazy loading, etc.
A proxy is a wrapper or agent object that the client calls to access the real serving object behind the scenes. Extra functionalities can be provided into proxy such as caching the operations on the actual object or checking pre-conditions before calling operations on the actual object. A proxy functions as an interface to something else.

When-to use:
  • When we need to perform additional operations (lazy loading, caching, access control) when accessing an object.
Components:
  • Subject (Interface) – Declares common interface for RealSubject and Proxy.
  • RealSubject – The actual object that does the work.
  • Proxy – Controls access to RealSubject, implements the same interface.
Real-world example:
  • Java RMI – Uses proxy to call remote objects.
  • Spring AOP – Uses proxies for method interception.
  • Hibernate – Lazy-loaded entities are proxies.
  • Security managers – Proxy access to critical resources.
  • Credit card - Acts as a proxy for our bank account.

title: Flyweight
content:
Flyweight pattern is a structural design pattern that reduces memory uses by sharing similar objects.
Flyweight pattern uses a factory to manage these shared objects and ensures that each object is created only once.
When we need large number of similar objects then creating and storing each object separately can take too much memory.

Components:
  • Flyweight interface – Declares methods that accept extrinsic state.
  • ConcreteFlyweight – Implements Flyweight and stores intrinsic state.
  • FlyweightFactory – Manages a pool of flyweight objects.
  • Client – Maintains or computes extrinsic state and passes it to the flyweight.
Pros and cons:
  • Reduces memory usage by sharing objects.
  • Increases performance when creating many similar objects.
  • Makes code more complex.
  • Requires careful separation of intrinsic and extrinsic state.

title: Decorator
content:
Decorator is a structural design pattern that allows us to add new behavior or functionality to objects dynamically without altering their structure or modifying their source code. This is achieved by creating decorator classes that wrap the original object and add new behaviours or attributes. Decorators provide a flexible alternative to subclassing for extending functionality. Decorator design pattern allows behaviours to be added to individual objects, either statically or dynamically without affecting the behaviour of other objects from the same class.

When-to use:
  • When we want to add responsibilities to individual objects, not an entire class.
  • When we want to keep classes open for extension but closed for modification.
Components:
  • Component: The interface or abstract class defining the operations.
  • Concrete component: The original object that we want to extend.
  • Decorator: Implements the same interface and has a reference to a Component object.
  • Concrete Decorators: Add new behaviors before or after delegating the request to the wrapped component.
Advantages:
  • Adheres to SRP and OCP.
  • Greater flexibility than static inheritance.
  • Can add or remove responsibilities at runtime.
Real-world examples:
  • Java IO Streams.
  • Spring's Transactional, Cacheable can be seen as decorators.
  • Spring Framework - Middleware or Interceptors decorate request and response handling.

title: Observer
content:
Observer pattern is a behavioral design pattern that defines a one-to-many dependency between objects.
In this pattern an object known as subject maintains a list of its dependent objects known as observers.
When the subject's state changes, all objects that depend on it are notified and updated automatically by subject.

When-to use:
  • Use Observer when you want to automatically notify multiple objects of state changes.
  • Great for event-driven systems, GUIs, distributed messaging, and real-time updates.
  • Think of it as a push-based notification system for objects.
Components:
  • Subject – The core object being observed. Maintains a list of observers.
  • Observer – Interface that defines the update method.
  • ConcreteSubject – Implements subject and notifies observers.
  • ConcreteObserver – Implements observer and responds to state changes.

title: Visitor
content:
Visitor is a behavioral design pattern that lets us add new operations to existing object structures without modifying their classes.
Useful in scenario when an object structure is stable but we frequently need to extend its behaviours with new operations.
Visitor pattern helps separate algorithms from the objects on which they operate.
Visitor pattern aligns with open-closed concepts.

Components:
  • Visitor – Interface or abstract class for visiting elements.
  • ConcreteVisitor – Implements operations on concrete elements.
  • Element – Interface that defines accept(visitor)
  • ConcreteElement – Implements accept(visitor)
  • Client – Traverses object structure and applies visitor.
Real-world examples:
  • Filesystem utilities – Backup, search, indexing tools can visit folders and files.
  • Game engines – Collision detection or rendering can be implemented as visitors over game entities.
  • AST traversal– Different visitors (semantic analyzer, code generator) operate on the same tree nodes.
  • Document converters – HTML, PDF, MD converters can visit document elements (paragraphs, images, links).
Pros and cons:
  • Add new operations without changing existing object structures.
  • Encourages separation of concerns (data vs behavior).
  • Makes operations extensible and easy to manage.
  • Adding a new element (type) requires updating all visitors.
  • Involves double dispatch – one call from client to element, one from element to visitor.

title: Mediator
content:
Mediator is a behavioral design pattern that promotes loose coupling between objects by centralizing communication between them. Instead of objects referring to each other directly, they communicate through a mediator object. This makes the system easier to maintain, modify, and scale, especially as the number of objects increases. Mediator pattern focuses on simplifying communication between objects by managing and coordinating their interations through a mediator. Mediator pattern is used for coordinating communication while the proxy pattern is used for controlling access.

Components:
  • Mediator interface: Declares the communication contract used by components.
  • ConcreteMediator: Implements coordination logic and knows all components (colleagues).
  • Colleague: Individual objects that communicate via mediator. Knows about the mediator but not other colleagues.
Pros and Cons:
  • Promotes low coupling between components.
  • Simplifies maintenance and enhances reusability.
  • Centralizes complex communications.
  • Mediator can become a God object if it gets too complex.
  • Too much logic inside the mediator can lead to poor scalability.

title: Iterator
content:
Iterator pattern is a behavioral design pattern that provides a way to access the elements of a collection (like a list, tree or graph) sequentially without exposing its underlying representation. Iterator pattern is used to traverse elements in a container.
Intent is to provide a standard way to traverse through a collection of objects without exposing its internal structure.
Iterator pattern decouples container traversal algorithms from containers.

Components:
  • Iterator (Interface) – declares the interface for accessing elements.
  • ConcreteIterator – implements the Iterator interface and keeps track of the current position.
  • Aggregate (Interface) – declares a method to return an iterator.
  • ConcreteAggregate – implements the method to return an iterator instance.
Advantages:
  • Separates collection traversal logic from collection data structure.
  • Uniform traversal for various types of collections.
  • Supports multiple iterations simultaneously.

title: COR
content:
CoR design pattern is a behavioral design pattern that decouples sender and receiver of a request by connecting multiple handlers in a chain. The request is then passed along the chain until it is processed by one of the handlers. When-to use: when we have multiple objects that can handle a request but the specific object that handles it is determined at runtime.

Components:
Handler interface: Declares a method for handling requests and a reference to the next handler.
ConcreteHandler: Handles requests it is responsible for or forwards them to the next handler.
Client: Sends the request to the first handler in the chain.
Workflow:
A client sends a request to the first handler in the chain, if the handler can handle it, it does.
Otherwise, it forwards the request to the next handler in the chain.
This continues until the request is handled or the end of the chain is reached.

title: Multithreading
content:
Multithreading is a process of executing multiple threads simultaneously.
Multithreaded programs are capable of doing more than one tasks in parallel.
Multithreading allows different parts of the program to execute simultaneously.
Applications that perform several tasks that are not dependent on one another benefit the most from multithreading.
Parallelism is about doing multiple tasks at once. Concurrency is about dealing with multiple tasks at once.
Multi-threaded program: multiple instructions are executed in parallel or atleast appear to be executed.

title: Thread
content:
A thread of execution is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a OS scheduler. Threads of a process share its executable code and the values of its dynamically allocated variables and non-thread-local global variables at any given time. Local primitive variables are thread-safe because each thread has separate stack memory. Local reference variables are not thread-safe because each thread share heap memory. A thread is a sequence of instructions within a program that can be executed independently of other code. Thread is a dispatchable unit of work, includes a processor context (program counter and stack pointer) and its own data area for a stack. Each thread is executing the same program code and shares the same data area and heap however each thread has it own stack containing local variables.

Eahc thread has a priority, thread scheduler uses priority to determine which thread should be allowed to execute.
Threads with higher priority are executed in preference to threads with lower priority.
When two threads have the same priority then JVM will execute them in FIFO order.
When multiple threads are ready to execute then JVM will selects and executes the Runnable thread which has the highest priority.

title: Race condition
content:
Race condition occurs when multiple threads try to update mutable shared data at the same time.
Two or more threads simultaneously reading data from the same object is not a problem.
When many threads are simultaneously try to update the same object then memory inconsistencies may arise.
When one thread is updating the object while the other is reading it then memory inconsistencies may arise.
  • Read-read sharing is safe.
  • Both read-write and write-write races are a problem.
When multiple threads try to modify a shared resource at the same time then the final outcome is non deterministic.
We must explicitly synchronize concurrent access to a shared resource in a multi-threaded environment.
When a thread enters synchronized code (calling the synchronized method of that object) it takes the lock on that object.
Thus other threads cannot enters synchronized code because there is only one lock per object.
Cached shared data causes a thread not to notice that data has been changed by the another thread.
Resources: Memory, files, network connections.
Solutions to race condition:
  • Locks-Mutexes: Ensure only one thread can access the shared data at a time, like a key to a room.
  • Atomic Operations: Operations that complete indivisibly, preventing interruption.
  • Semaphores-Monitors: Other synchronization tools to control access to resources.
Examples
Bank Account Two people withdraw money from the same account at once. Without locks, both might read the balance, one withdraws, then the second withdraws, potentially leaving the account overdrawn or losing one withdrawal's record. Movie Ticket Suppose you are buying theatre tickets online and after you pick your seats and are entering your credit card information, someone else buys that seat and they are no longer available. Suppose multiple threads have access to a collection object and they are adding and removing at same time then there will be an error unless the collection is thread-safe. Document Editing Two users edit the same document. One saves changes, but before they're fully synced, the other saves, overwriting the first user's work. Shared Counter Two threads try to increment a counter variable.

title: Reactive
content:
Reactive programming is a declarative programming paradigm concerned with data streams and the propagation of change.
Reactive programming allows applications to react to updates automatically and efficiently.
Like reacting to something when user clicks this button run this function or when file IO operation is complete run this function. Imperative means when we are doing all the steps.
While declarative is where we are declaring this is what i want to happen and something is going to make that happen.
An imperative approach involves explicitly writing out the sequence of steps to achieve a result.
While a declarative approach describes the desired outcome and the programming language figures out the execution.
Main purpose of reactive programming is to avoid blocking in our code.

Synchronous = Sequential
Asynchronous = Non-sequential

List<Person> findByName(String name) -> void findByName(String name, Callback<List<Person>> callback)
BigDecimal getIncome(String name) -> void getIncome(String name, Callback<BigDecimal> callback)

title: Thread Pool
content:
Thread pool is a collection of pre-created worker threads that are kept ready to perform tasks.
Thread pool avoids the overhead of creating and destroying new threads for each task.
When a task is submitted, it is assigned to an available thread from the pool.
When all threads are busy, the task waits in a queue until a thread becomes free.
Thread pools improve performance by reusing threads and manage resources by limiting the no of threads running concurrently.

Key characteristics:
  • Worker threads: A set of threads that are created at the start and are always ready to execute tasks.
  • Task queue: A queue to hold tasks when all threads in the pool are busy.
  • Configurable: Thread pools allow configuration of the no. of threads, type of queue to use and how to handle rejected tasks.
How it works:
  • Task submission: Tasks are submitted to the thread pool, not directly to individual threads.
  • Task assignment: An available worker thread from the pool is assigned to the task.
  • Queueing: If all threads are busy, the task is placed in a waiting queue.
  • Thread reuse: After completing a task, the thread returns to the pool to wait for another task, instead of being terminated.
Advantages:
  • Improved performance: Reduces the significant cost of creating and destroying threads for each task.
  • Resource management: Limits the total no. of threads, preventing the system from running out of resources like memory.
  • Simplified programming: Developers can focus on the task logic rather than the complexities of managing thread lifecycles.

title: Monitor
content:
Synchronization is built around an internal entity known as the monitor.
Monitors are used to achieved mutual exclusion and threads cooperation.
A monitor is an entity that possesses a lock, a wait-queue and an entry-queue.
Every Java objects has a monitor associated with them.
Lock enforces mutual exclusive access to synchronized code block or method invoked on the associated object.
Entry-set is the set of all the threads who has already requested for the lock and the lock is not acquired by them yet.
Wait-set is the set of all the threads waiting on an monitor object that is used to provide coordination between multiple threads.

A lock is a tool for controlling access to a shared resource by multiple threads.
Every objects in java has an intrinsic lock associated with it.
Only one thread at a time can acquire the lock and all access to the shared resource requires that the lock be acquired first.
When a new thread tries to acquire the lock and if already a thread owns the lock then that thread will be waiting on the entry set to acquire the lock. When the thread which is acquired the lock completes execution of its critical section then it will release the lock. Next thread will acquire the lock but this next thread is taken from the entry set and will be determined by JVM based on some criteria like FIFO.

title: Mutual exclusion
content:
Mutual exclusion is a property of concurrency control, which is instituted for the purpose of preventing race conditions.
Race condition occures when a shared resource is accessed by different actors at the same time.
Both mutex and semaphore helps managing access to shared resources but they do it in different ways.
Mutex is suited for exclusive access whereas semaphore is suited for limited concurrency.
Mutual exclusion helps keep threads from interfering with each other while sharing data.
Mutual exclusion ensures that only one thread can have access to shared data at a time.
Mutual exclusion or atomicity ensures that write functionality is thread-safe.
Mutex is a program object which prevents simultaneous access to a shared data by multiple threads.
Critical section is region of the code where shared data between multiple threads is accessed.
Shared data is considered as a critical area.

Mutual exclusion can be achieved through:
  • Synchronized block
  • Synchronized method
  • Static synchronization

title: Deadlock
content:
A deadlock occurs when there is more than one thread, each waiting for a resource held by another.
Which occurs when multiple threads acquires the same set of lock in different order.
The most obvious kind of resource is an object monitor but any resource that causes blocking such as wait-notify can qualify.

Deadlock happens when two or more threads become interlocked:
  • Thread A holds the lock in object1 but is waiting on object2
  • Thread B holds the lock in object2 but is waiting on object1

title: Synchronization
content:
Synchronization is a mechanism which ensures that two or more concurrent processes or threads do not simultaneously execute some particular program segment known as critical section.Processes' access to critical section is controlled by using synchronization techniques. When one thread starts executing the critical section (serialized segment of the program) the other thread should wait until the first thread finishes. There is no any guarantee about exactly when a blocked thread is unblocked when the synchronized block is free again. This is typically up to the OS or execution platform to coordinate the unblocking of blocked threads. Thread synchronization is a mechanism which ensures that two or more concurrent threads do not execute some particular section of program especially critical section. There are two types of thread synchronization mutual exclusion and inter-thread communication.

Following are some classic problems of synchronization:
  • Producer-consumer problem
  • Readers-writers problem
  • Dining philosopher problem
Thread cooperation is achieved using the wait-set which is associated with the monitor and wait-notify mechanism.
Cooperation is important when one thread needs some data to be in a particular state and another thread is responsible for getting the data into that state.

When a thread invokes the wait method respect to an object then the thread will be suspended and added to the wait-set to wait until some other thread invokes notify or notifyAll on the same object. If a thread was put in the queue by a call to wait then it must be unfrozen by a call to notify before it can be scheduled for execution again.
Notify method is used for waking up threads that are in the wait-set of the monitor of a particular object.
A thread may call wait, notify or notifyAll on an object only if it owns the monitor lock of that object.

title: Synchronized
content:
A block of code marked with synchronized becomes a synchronized block.
Keyword synchronized enforces exclusive access to the block of code.
Only one thread is allowed to enter this block of code at the same time.
Thread that first enters the synchronized block remains in runnable state.
Synchronized blocks and synchronized methods are mutually exclusive.
Synchronized method can be static method or instance method.
The synchronized keyword does not support fairness.
Fairness property provides a lock to the longest waiting thread (contention).
Any thread can acquire lock once released, no preference can be specified.
All other threads accessing the same block of code enters the blocked state.
When a runnable thread exits the synchronized block then lock is released.
Another thread is now allowed to enter the runnable state and place a new lock.

When two or more threads modify an object then declare the methods that carry out the modification as synchronized.
When a thread wants to execute a synchronized method on a given object, first it has to acquire the lock of that object.
Once thread acquired the lock then it is allowed to execute any synchronized method on that object.
When a thread calls a synchronized method on an object then the JVM ckecks the monitor lock for that object.
When the monitor lock is unowned then ownership is assigned to the calling thread which is then allowed to proceed with call.
When the monitor lock is owned by another thread then the calling thread will be put on hold until the lock becomes available.
When a thread exits a synchronized method it releases the monitor lock, allowing a waiting thread to proceed.
When a class has one or more synchronized methods, each object of the class gets a queue that holds all threads waiting to execute one of the synchronized methods.
